chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him) regarding discouragement from the world and encouragement for the Hereafter.
The world is a place of departure, and it is not a place of permanence, so make it the target of the Hereafter, and take from it provisions for tomorrow.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the nature of the world in relation to the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the concept of *al-zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a strategic detachment to prioritize the eternal Hereafter over the fleeting world. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing worldly duties with spiritual preparation, urging believers to treat the world as a 'harvest field' for the afterlife rather than an end in itself. Such guidance underscores the practical application of Quranic principles in daily life, encouraging Muslims to accumulate good deeds as provisions for their ultimate return to God.

en.sayed-ali-raza: and importance of collecting provisions for the next life
